findings.title: _slot_wait_event_s accepts NaN/inf from the environment
findings.detail: _float_env rejects values that are not finite, but _slot_wait_event_s does not. With NW_WORKER_SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_S=inf the slot_wait frame never goes out. With NaN, `v >= 0` is False, so the code falls back to the default. Only an operator or test env var can set this, so the risk is negligible.
findings.suggested_fix: In worker.py, have _slot_wait_event_s return _float_env(SLOT_WAIT_ENV, gate_slots.WAIT_EVENT_S) so it shares the finite/non-negative check.
findings.acceptance: A unit test with NW_WORKER_SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_S=inf gets back gate_slots.WAIT_EVENT_S.

findings.title: NW_CONFIG_DIR is set to an empty string when cfg has no config_dir
findings.detail: _run_gates sets NW_CONFIG_DIR to str(cfg.get('config_dir') or ''). A gate would then see NW_CONFIG_DIR='' instead of the variable being unset, and that could make tools that read it look at the cwd.
findings.suggested_fix: Add NW_CONFIG_DIR to env only when cfg.get('config_dir') is truthy.
findings.acceptance: With no config_dir in cfg, a gate running `env` prints no NW_CONFIG_DIR= line.

ac_assessment.ac: Piping a valid header and bundle runs the gates and emits accepted, started, one gate frame per gate (.log/.json/.r<n>), done
ac_assessment.evidence: test_pass_emits_frames_and_files checks that the frame types are exactly [accepted, started, gate, done] and that the files are {.log, .json}. test_retry_ladder_sends_r1_files checks for the .r1.log/.r1.json files. Code: worker.gate_job, _run_gates, gate_files.

ac_assessment.ac: git merge-base $NW_BASE HEAD on the worker prints the coordinator's sha
ac_assessment.evidence: test_merge_base_and_base_placeholder_match_the_coordinator compares against `git merge-base main HEAD` run in the source repo. test_origin_base_name_resolves_like_a_remote_tracking_branch covers an origin/main base. Code: _checkout creates refs/heads/<name> and refs/remotes/origin/<rest> in the private clone.

ac_assessment.ac: An env key outside the allowlist gives error stage validate and nothing runs; a reused job_id gives stage claim
ac_assessment.evidence: test_env_outside_allowlist_is_refused checks rc 3, stage validate, frames == [error] and that the marker file was not created. test_duplicate_job_id_is_a_claim_error checks stage claim and that the first job's frames.jsonl is unchanged. Code: validate_header, and the exclusive mkdir in gate_job.

ac_assessment.ac: Two concurrent jobs, same repo_key and base.name with different base.sha, each see their own base
ac_assessment.evidence: In test_concurrent_jobs_see_their_own_base, two jobs synchronise on a shared dir (slots: 2) so they really run at the same time, and each one's log holds its own base sha twice. Code: git clone --shared gives each job private refs.

ac_assessment.ac: EOF mid-gate ends the gate process and gives done interrupted; EOF during the slot wait gives done interrupted with no started
ac_assessment.evidence: test_eof_mid_gate_interrupts checks that the sleep child's pid is dead, interrupted is true and the next gate never ran. test_eof_while_waiting_for_the_slot checks for no started or gate frame and no marker file. Code: _watch_stdin, and cancel passed as stop= to gate_slots.acquire.

ac_assessment.ac: With the slot held elsewhere, slot_wait then started only once the slot frees
ac_assessment.evidence: test_held_slot_gives_slot_wait_then_started holds GS.acquire, checks that no started frame appears while the slot is held, then checks the order accepted, slot_wait, started, gate, done. It uses NW_WORKER_SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_S through _slot_conf.

ac_assessment.ac: Exit 0 after done (pass, fail, interrupted) and 3 after error
ac_assessment.evidence: The pass, fail, EOF and signal tests assert rc 0. The validate, claim, checkout and read error tests assert rc 3. Code: gate_job/_fail return 0 or EXIT_ERROR, and cli_worker raises SystemExit with that code.

ac_assessment.ac: A log over 16 MiB arrives cut to 16 MiB with truncated_bytes
ac_assessment.evidence: test_log_over_16_mib_is_truncated checks that len == MAX_LOG_BYTES, the tail marker is kept, the head marker is cut, and truncated_bytes is exact. Code: _file_payload, gate_files.

ac_assessment.ac: have reports commit and base after the job; after gc --keep-days 0 nothing is reported, cat-file -e fails, job dirs are gone; a live job's dir survives
ac_assessment.evidence: test_have_then_gc_removes_refs_objects_and_job_dirs runs the real CLI have and gc, then checks that git cat-file -e fails and the job dir is gone. test_gc_during_a_live_job_keeps_its_dir checks that the tree and the commit object survive. Code: have, gc, _gc_repo, _live_jobs.

ac_assessment.ac: nw worker info --json prints the documented keys
ac_assessment.evidence: test_info_json_keys checks that the key set is exactly {schema, protocol, version, git_sha, data_dir, git, uv, free_bytes}.

ac_assessment.ac: ssh-command execs the four allowed subcommands and refuses everything else with exit 2
ac_assessment.evidence: In tests/test_worker_ssh_command.py, test_allowed_commands_are_execd patches only os.execvp and covers six forms. test_refused_commands_run_nothing covers 24+ refusals, including `have --repo ../x`. The CLI subprocess tests check exit 2 with `refused:` and that an allowed command really execs. Code: check_ssh_command, own_nw, ssh_command.

ac_assessment.ac: docs/WORKFLOW.md documents the mandatory dedicated user and the absolute-path key line
ac_assessment.evidence: The WORKFLOW.md section 'Remote gate worker' has both. test_workflow_docs_make_the_dedicated_user_mandatory_and_show_the_key_line checks for them.
